name: Russian Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1800 polygon "Russian Empire" = 16.35M km2 on the sphere; add Finland (1809, ~0.38M), Bessarabia (1812, ~0.045M), Georgia and Russian America (~1.5M claimed, thinly held).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1816 = 45,900k, which includes Congress Poland (~3.3M, joined 1815). Without it ~42.5M for 1812; includes Finland (1809) and Bessarabia (May 1812).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) Russia (modern borders) 1810 = 1.9%; Baltic and Polish-Lithuanian provinces were more urban. Towns of 5,000+ ~3-6%.

activePersonnel.note: Regulars plus Cossacks in service, June 1812. Page: 571,000-713,000 Russians committed during 1812 (Bodart, Sokolov); first wave on the western frontier 198,000 (Riehn); second line 129,000 + 8,000 Cossacks with 434 guns; plus the Danube army, Finland, Caucasus and interior garrisons. Opolchenie excluded (reserves).

trainedReserves.note: Third line of 36 recruit depots and militias ~161,000 (page) plus the opolchenie raised by the July 1812 manifesto (~200,000-300,000, Lieven, Russia Against Napoleon ch. 5). Militia were serf levies with pikes and little training.

supportPersonnel.note: Field and garrison artillery ~40,000, pioneers ~5,000, navy (Baltic and Black Sea) ~30,000, train and staff ~10,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Page: Russian army reached its peak 1812 strength of 904,000 after reinforcements; with ~200,000-300,000 opolchenie ~1.1-1.2M of ~42M = 2.6-2.9%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Guard, grenadier, line and garrison infantry; first-wave armies (198,000 total, Riehn via French invasion page) were ~70% infantry, the rest in second line, Danube, Finland, Caucasus and garrisons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: muskets of 28 calibres, poor powder; bayonet emphasis

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: 25-year service, steady in defence (Borodino)

count.note: 50 jaeger regiments of 2 battalions at ~600 present each.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: some rifled carbines, mostly muskets

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: skirmish drill improved after 1807 but below French standard

count.note: Guard heavy cavalry and 8 cuirassier regiments.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: good heavy horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional long-service troopers

count.note: Regular dragoons, hussars and uhlans (~45,000) plus Cossacks in service (~50,000 with the field armies; page: the 428,000 who came into action include more than 80,000 Cossacks and militiamen).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Cossack ponies and lances, regular light horse adequate

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Cossacks superb at raiding and screening, useless in line

count.note: Field guns: the three western armies ~940, second line 434 (page), Danube army and reserves. Borodino: ~640 Russian guns.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 1805 Arakcheev system, unicorn howitzers, heavy 12-pdr batteries

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: numerous and brave gunners, reserve artillery handled clumsily at Borodino

count.note: Educated guess: ships of the line on the Baltic and Black Sea lists, many in poor repair; frigates counted as minor.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: rot-prone pine hulls

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little sea time; Senyavin's Mediterranean squadron (1805-07) the exception

count.note: Educated guess: frigates, brigs and the Baltic rowing gunboat flotillas.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: skerry gunboats suited to the Finnish coast

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscript crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Barclay de Tolly's retreat strategy, Kutuzov, Bagration; divided command and court intrigue until August

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: serf soldiers cut off from home for 25 years; regiment as family

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: defence of the homeland and Orthodoxy; rose to existential after Smolensk

weapons.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: artillery at the anchor, small arms below it

ships.note: Anchor: 6 (74-gun ships of the line). Evidence: sail fleet, weaker build quality

fortification.note: Anchor: 6 (Vauban-type forts). Evidence: Riga, Bobruisk, Dinaburg works incomplete; Smolensk old walls

logistics.note: Anchor: 6 (magazines + requisition). Evidence: magazine system along the Dvina and Dnieper; scorched-earth denial

communications.note: Anchor: 6 (semaphore telegraph). Evidence: no optical telegraph network until the 1830s; couriers

isr.note: Anchor: 6 (1805). Evidence: Cossack screens, Chernyshev's espionage in Paris (French invasion page)

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: No Maddison value for Russia before 1860. Analogues (Maddison 2023 via OWID): Russia 1860 = 754, USSR-area 1860 = 1,525, Poland 1815-1820 = 733-818, Finland 1820 = 1,313. Assumes little growth 1812-1860.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: army and navy took over half of state spending in 1812 (assignat-financed); state budget ~10% of output.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: over 90% of the population rural; Urals iron and Tula arms works.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: peasant agriculture near subsistence; grain exports from the south.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. Recruit levies took only ~1-2 men per 500 souls per year in peace, 1812 levies far more.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Tula, Petrozavodsk and Lugansk foundries field-gun output per year in 1812-13.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ships of the line launched per year at Petersburg, Arkhangelsk and Nikolaev.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: post roads; few engineered chaussees before the 1817 Petersburg-Moscow road.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Petersburg/Kronstadt, Riga, Reval, Arkhangelsk, Odessa, Sevastopol, Kherson/Nikolaev, Taganrog.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: small merchant fleet; most Russian trade carried in foreign hulls.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: magazine-based armies falling back on their own depots.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: peasant horses and oxen of European Russia.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: deep strategic depth and a harsh climate the invader was not adapted to; the 1812 campaign is the textbook case.

notes: Snapshot = Russian Empire on 24 June 1812 as the Grande Armee crossed the Neman. Population and territory = the Empire incl. Finland and Bessarabia, excluding Congress Poland (1815) and Russian America's native population; includes is empty. Personnel: regulars and Cossacks in service = active; recruit depots and the 1812 opolchenie = trainedReserves. Strength range for 1812 from the French invasion of Russia page (Bodart, Riehn, Sokolov, Lieven); branch split is a reconstruction, grade C. COW data begin 1816; 1816 used as anchor. No Maddison series for Russia before 1860.
